extracted.intended_audience: immigration attorneys and legal organizations preparing rulemaking comments
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting substantive, technical public comments on proposed or final immigration regulations (notice-and-comment rulemaking) on behalf of attorneys or legal organizations. Emphasis on legal analysis, evidentiary support, and proposed alternative regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of AILA (37,000 lawyers) and the Council
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open the letter by identifying AILA (and membership size) and the co-signing organization to establish representativeness, expertise, and stakeholder standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Letter Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint letter identification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state that the submission is a joint letter (when applicable) to convey coalition support and broader institutional endorsement of the positions taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject Line with Docket and Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line with specific docket and rule
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the exact docket number and rule title in the subject line so the comment is properly associated with the rulemaking record and easily located by agency staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Authority Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory authority analysis - whether agency has power under INA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether the agency has statutory authority under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) to enact the proposed change; cite the specific INA provisions that authorize or limit agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutional analysis - due process, equal protection issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate potential constitutional issues such as due process and equal protection, explaining how the rule may violate constitutional standards and supporting arguments with precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural analysis - APA notice, comment, logical outgrowth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the agency complied with the Administrative Procedure Act (adequate notice, meaningful opportunity to comment) and doctrines like logical outgrowth; explain procedural defects and potential remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Impact Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical impact - case management, asylum processing, detention conditions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe real-world operational consequences of the rule on case management, asylum processing timelines, detention conditions, and other programmatic operations to demonstrate concrete harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Empirical Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical data - case statistics, processing times, denial rates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with empirical evidence (case statistics, processing times, denial rates). Cite reliable data sources and quantify impacts where possible to bolster credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative analysis - prior administration practices, other countries
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the proposal to prior administration practices, historical norms, or practices in other countries to contextualize departures and implications for policy coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section-by-Section Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific section-by-section comments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted, clause-level critique of each regulatory provision being amended or added to show precise legal and practical problems; reference exact regulatory text and cite supporting authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested Alternative Regulatory Text
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested alternative regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include proposed replacement language or edits to regulatory text to give the agency workable alternatives and to demonstrate constructive engagement rather than only criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Specific INA Provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific INA provisions (8 USC § 1101, 1158, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the exact statutory provisions in the INA that are implicated (for example, 8 U.S.C. § 1101, § 1158) to anchor arguments in statutory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Affected CFR Provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference 8 CFR provisions being amended
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and cite the exact 8 C.F.R. sections that the rule would change, to make clear the rule's regulatory footprint and facilitate cross-referencing in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Federal Court Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite federal court decisions (BIA, AAO, federal district/circuit, Supreme Court)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support legal claims with controlling and persuasive precedent from the BIA, AAO, federal district and circuit courts, and the Supreme Court as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite International Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite the Convention Against Torture and other international obligations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring treaty obligations and international law (e.g., CAT) into the analysis where the rule implicates nonrefoulement or other international standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Case Examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific case examples (anonymized as needed)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate harms and practical effects with anonymized client examples or representative case vignettes while protecting confidentiality and privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Attorney-Client Representation Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Address attorney-client representation impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the rule will affect attorneys' ability to represent clients (e.g., timeline burdens, access to records, ability to prepare cases) and the resulting effects on access to justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Agency Performance Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite EOIR and USCIS performance data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use agency-supplied metrics (EOIR/USCIS backlog, processing times, dispositions) to show likely operational consequences and to counter speculative agency claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss Immigration Court Backlog
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with immigration court backlog and processing times
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how the rule will affect existing backlogs and processing capacity, and tie these effects to due process and access-to-counsel concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference ORR Shelter Capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Office of Refugee Resettlement and ORR shelter capacity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address downstream service impacts such as ORR shelter capacity to show broader systemic consequences beyond adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Service Center Processing Implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Address Service Center processing implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider and describe how changes will affect service centers, administrative processing, and other non-court operational units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight Concrete Consequences of Rule Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight concrete consequences e.g., shortened appeal times, summary dismissal defaults, burdens on counsel, caseload shifts to federal courts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out specific procedural changes (for example, IFR shortening appeal time to 10 days, making summary dismissal the default) and explain how each change will burden counsel, lead to incomplete records, and shift litigation to federal courts; use recent rule examples to illustrate points.
